memory_update.text: ATI is the reference benchmark for specialty materials, titanium alloys, superalloys, forgings, and aerospace/defense exposure, but it is now too visible/large to be the main underfollowed discovery target.

IPX is the cleanest domestic titanium traceability candidate found in this pass because its disclosed U.S. government funding is explicitly tied to reshoring titanium supply for defense industrial-base needs.
MTRN is a second-order specialty-materials candidate; later work must prove whether aerospace/defense material provenance and qualification barriers are material enough to the thesis.
SIF is a speculative-shadow candidate: direct public evidence supports aerospace/defense forgings and machining, but domestic raw-material traceability upside remains unproven.

Need a focused Layer 2 evidence pass on certifications, customer concentration, DFARS/Buy America clauses, domestic raw-material origin controls, and whether primes are actually reshuffling suppliers over material traceability.

summary: Expanded the universe around domestic aerospace/defense material traceability with a two-lane funnel. The reference lane uses ATI as a larger, more visible specialty-materials anchor. The underfollowed lane prioritizes narrower public assets tied to domestic titanium, specialty metals, beryllium/alloys, forgings, machined components, and quality-certified aerospace supply. Key uncertainty: direct evidence of prime-contractor supplier-audit share shifts is still weak; later layers should verify customer qualification, DFARS/Buy America exposure, domestic feedstock documentation, and whether working-capital/capex needs dilute the benefit.
